simple.meaning: דּוּכִיפַת (dûwkîyphath) is a Hebrew word meaning “the hoopoe or else the grouse.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דּוּכִיפַת (H1744) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 11:19, with occurrences in Leviticus, Deuteronomy.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוּכִיפַת (H1744) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דּוּכִיפַת (H1744) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דּוּכִיפַת (dûwkîyphath) / H1744 is traced through Leviticus 11:19, Deuteronomy 14:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: the hoopoe or else the grouse
definitions.full: H1744. dukiphath דּוּכִיפַת noun feminine an unclean bird , perhaps hoopoe, ᵑ9 ᵐ5 Saad and others (compare Di Kn Lev 11:19 ) 11:19 ; Deut 14:18 . ** דּוּכִיפַת , name of bird: possibly of Egyptian origin, Bondi ZMG 1 {1896}, 292 (Arabic, Ol § 221 compare Kö ET ix {1898}, 476 ). דום (Late Hebrew דום spread slander , perhaps originally whisper , compare דממה דמם, ).

occurrences.englishText: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
the stork, the heron after its kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
